title: Chinese intervention in the Korean War
summary: On 19 October 1950, as United Nations forces pushed north through Korea, Chinese People's Volunteers crossed the Yalu River in force after Mao Zedong set that evening as the deadline; some advance elements had entered a couple of days earlier. China's entry halted the UN advance and turned a limited conflict into a much longer war.

uncertainty.note: Chen Jian (Wilson Center) writes that Mao set the evening of 19 October as the deadline for crossing, while a regiment of the Forty-second Army entered Korea early on 17 October; the army.mil timeline also files the entry under 19 October. First crossings span 17-19 October.

as_recorded.value: On 19 October 1950, Chinese troops crossed the Yalu.

where.modern_name: Yalu River crossings at Dandong (China) and Sinuiju (North Korea)
where.historical_name: Yalu River border between Manchuria (People's Republic of China) and North Korea

importance.justification: China's entry transformed the Korean War from a UN advance into a prolonged conflict and shaped Cold War alignments in East Asia.

related.because: The war that Chinese entry prolonged ended only with the July 1953 armistice.

sources.title: The Sino-Soviet Alliance and China's Entry into the Korean War (CWIHP Working Paper No. 1)
sources.publisher: Woodrow Wilson International Center for Scholars

reviewer_note: Least sure of the exact crossing date: Chen Jian describes units crossing from 17 October and a 19 October deadline. The army.mil page gives only a timeline entry for 19 October, and the pin is a border stretch, not one crossing point.

beats.caption: On the evening Mao set as the deadline, Chinese People's Volunteers began crossing the Yalu River into North Korea.
Chinese forces went on to defeat outnumbered United Nations units and inflict heavy casualties, widening the war.
